:Judgment:

1. The petitioner filed this petition under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act 1989, seeking compensation of Rs.15,00,000/- for the injures sustained by her in the road traffic accident occurred on 19.04.2024.
2.

It is the case of the petitioner that, on 19.04.2024 at about 5.30 p.m., within the jurisdiction of Ramasamudram Police Station, near Yembadi Tank, Punganuru - Ramasamudram Road,
Kudurucheemanapalli, Ramasamudram Mandal, when the driver of the unoffending Auto bearing Reg. No.AP-03-X-4197 drove the same along with Petitioner and other passengers, at that time the driver of the offending Swift Dzire Car bearing Reg. No.AP-28-CD-8757 drove the same in a high speed, 3 SCCH - 7 M.V.C.No.9530/2024 rash and negligent manner so as to endangering human life and dashed against the unoffending vehicle, as a result, the unoffending vehicle became turtle/upside on the middle of the road, as a result the passengers and the Petitioner has sustained grievous injuries.

Thereafter Petitioner was shifted to Government Hospital, Punganur and for higher treatment she was shifted to Sahasra Hospital, Punganur wherein she was treated as inpatient from 19.04.2024 to 22.04.2024.
She has spent Rs.2,00,000/- towards medical expenditure and other incidental charges.
In this regard the informant/Pavani Chinnagangannagari Pavani has lodged complaint before the Ramasamudram police station.

Accordingly, a case was registered in their Crime No.87/2024 and prepared F.I.R. for the offence punishable under sections 338 and 337 of IPC and submitted to the jurisdictional judicial Magistrate and the superior officers and investigation was taken up by the investigating Officer.

3. Further it is contended that, prior to the alleged accident the Petitioner was hale, healthy and she was aged about 34 years and she was doing mason assistant work and earning sum of Rs.30,000/-
p.m. 4 SCCH - 7 M.V.C.No.9530/2024 Due to the injuries sustained in the alleged accident he lost her income and future prospective life, happiness, and earning capacity and become disabled and dependent.
The alleged accident is occurred due to fault and negligence act of the driver of the offending Maruthi Swift Dezire Car bearing Reg. No.AP-28-CD-8757.
Respondent No.1 is the RC owner and Respondent No.2 is the Insurer of the said offending vehicle, as such the respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to Petitioner.
Hence Petitioner filed the present claim petition for seeking compensation.

4. In response to the notice, the Respondents No.1 and 2 have appeared before the court through their counsels and Respondent No.1 has not filed the written statement and the Respondent No.2 has filed their written statement.

2 5.

In the written statement of respondent No.2, Respondent No.2 the Insurance Company has admitting that, the offending Maruthi Swift Dezire Car bearing Reg. No.AP-28-CD-8757 was duly insured with it and the same is valid on the date of the accident and denied the petition averments in part.
Further it has contended that the insured vehicle is not involved in the accident.
The insurer 5 SCCH - 7 M.V.C.No.9530/2024 liability is subjected to validity of the DL and other documents as per the law.

Further it is alleged that there is no compliance of provision under Section 134(C),
158(6) of M.V. Act.
Further it is contended that the alleged accident is occurred due to fault of the driver of the unoffending Auto and no fault of the driver of the offending vehicle.
As such the insurance company is not liable to pay any compensation and in order to get compensation the Petitioner has constrained to filed the present claim petition.

Further it is denied that the age,
income and occupation of the Petitioner and the petition is false and frivolous in the eye of law and the quantum of compensation claimed by the claimants is exorbitant and reserves the right u/s.170 of M.V. Act., and violated terms and conditions of the insurance policy.
Hence sought for dismissal of the claim petition.
6. On the basis of above pleadings following Issues were framed.

:: I S S U E S ::
1.

Whether the Petitioner proves that on 19-04-2024 at about 5.30 p.m., when she was going towards Punganur town from Ramasamudram town side as a passenger in a Auto Rickshaw 6 SCCH - 7 M.V.C.No.9530/2024 bearing registration No.AP-03-X-  4197 near Yemabadi Village,
 Ramasamudram Mandal,
 Annamayya district, Andhra Pradesh, at that time the driver of the said offending Maruthi Dezire Car bearing registration No.AP-28- CD-8757 drove the same in a high speed, rash and negligent manner and dashed against the said Auto Rickshaw and as a result the Auto Rickshaw capsized and she sustained grievous injuries?
2. Whether petitioner is entitled for compensation? If so, what is the quantum?

from whom?
3. What order or award?

7. In order to prove the case of petitioner, petitioner got examined himself as PW-1 and got marked Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.11 and Dr.S.A. Somashekara got examined as Pw.2 and got marked Ex.P.12 and Ex.P.13 and closed their side.
The Insurance Company got examined its Senior Executive as RW-1 and got marked Ex.R.1 and Ex.R.2 and closed their side.
8. Heard the arguments from both side.

9. My findings to the above referred Issues are as under:

3 7 SCCH - 7 M.V.C.No.9530/2024 Issue No.1 :- In the affirmative Issue No.2 :- Partly in the affirmative Issue No.3 :- As per final order, for the following.......
:REASONS:
10. Issue No.1:- This petition is filed u/s.166 of M.V.Act 1989 for seeking compensation for the injuries sustained by the Petitioner in the alleged accident.
11.

The petitioner in the petition has contended that, on 19.04.2024 at about 5.30 p.m., within the jurisdiction of Ramasamudram Police Station, near Yembadi Tank, Punganuru - Ramasamudram Road, Kudurucheemanapalli, Ramasamudram Mandal, when the driver of the unoffending Auto bearing Reg. No.AP-03-X-4197 drove the same along with Petitioner and other passengers, at that time the driver of the offending Swift Dzire Car bearing Reg. No.AP-28-CD-8757 drove the same in a high speed, rash and negligent manner so as to endangering human life and dashed against the unoffending vehicle, as a result, the unoffending vehicle became turtle/upside on the middle of the road, as a result the passengers and the Petitioner has sustained grievous injuries.

Thereafter Petitioner was shifted to Government Hospital, Punganur and for higher 8 SCCH - 7 M.V.C.No.9530/2024 treatment she was shifted to Sahasra Hospital, Punganur wherein she was treated as inpatient from 19.04.2024 to 22.04.2024.
It is contended that the alleged accident was occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle.

The Respondent No.2 admitted the alleged accident and its version is that, the alleged accident occurred due to the negligence and fault of the driver of the unoffending vehicle and no fault of the driver of the offending vehicle, however, slowly he may be driving and therefore he cannot be held to be negligent.
Further it is alleged that, driver of the offending vehicle is not possessing valid D.L, at the time of alleged accident.
As such the insurance company is not liable to pay any compensation and in order to obtain the compensation Petitioner has constrained to filed the present claim petition.

Further it is denied that the age, income and occupation of the Petitioner and the petition is false and frivolous in the eye of law and the quantum of compensation claimed by the claimants is exorbitant and sought for dismissal of the petition.
12.
The burden to prove the framed issues lies on the Petitioner.

Hence, in order to prove her case,
the Petitioner herself examined as P.W.1 and she has 9 SCCH - 7 M.V.C.No.9530/2024 reiterated the entire petition averments and contentions taken in the course of claim petition in his evidence before this Court and also produced as many as Exs.P.1 to P.11 documents.
Therefore, there is no necessity to repeat those facts again.

In support of the Petitioner's case and in order to substantiate the oral evidence of P.W.1, the Petitioner has examined one witness by name Dr.S.A. Somashekara,
as PW.2.
I have gone through the documents produced by the PW-1.
Ex. P-1
is the copy of FIR,

Ex.P.2 is the Statment/Complaint, Ex.P.2(a) is the translated copy of Ex.P.2, Ex.P.3 is her statement, Ex.P.3(a) is the translated copy of Ex.P.3, Ex.P.4 is the Spot Sketch, Ex.P.4(a) is the translated copy of Ex.P.4, Ex.P.5 is the Wound Certificate, Ex.P.6 is the Charge Sheet, Ex.P.7 is the Discharge Summary, Ex.P.8 is the OPD Sheets, Ex.P.9 is the Lab Reports, Ex.P.10 is the Medical Bills , Ex.P.11 is the Adhar Card.

Sujatha B vs Krishnakumar C on 2 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/6281331/
4 13.

In the cross-examination of PW-1 by the counsel for Respondent No.2, she has deposed that,
after completion of their work they were proceeding in the unoffending Auto towards their house.
There was 13 passengers were traveling in the said auto.
She sat at the side of the auto.

Further she has denied that 10 SCCH - 7 M.V.C.No.9530/2024 due to carrying of excess passengers in the said auto, the driver of the auto has lost control and due to his fault caused the alleged accident and the same is not due to fault of the offending vehicle.

When they are proceeding in the auto, the offending car was following the auto and dashed against the said auto, as a result she and other passenger were sustained injuries and she has sustained grievous injuries on her legs and hands.

After the alleged accident she was shifted to Government Hospital, Punganur and for higher treatment she was shifted to Government Madanapalli and thereafter for higher treatment she was shifted to Sahasra Hospital, Madanapalli and she has undergone surgery therein.
She has informed to the hospital regarding the alleged incident.
Further she has denied that she is hale and healthy and she is doing her work and other activities as past without any pain or difficulties.
Further she has denied that she has not suffering pain or difficulties while climbing steps, walking, sitting.
Further she has deposed that prior to the alleged accident she was doing mason work and earning Rs.700/- per day and due to alleged accident she is not able to do any work.
Further she has denied that she has not incurred Rs.1,00,000/- towards her medical expenditure.

Further she has 11 SCCH - 7 M.V.C.No.9530/2024 denied that in order to get more compensation in collusion with the police she has falsely implicated the driver of the offending vehicle and registered false case against him and she has produced concocted created documents and filed false evidence affidavit and deposing falsely.
During the cross examination Pw.1 has consistently deposed on the lines of the petition/prosecution case and she has made those versions, which could not be shattered in cross examination.

14. In order to prove the version of Respondent No.2, the Respondent No.2 has examined its Senior Executive as RW-1 and she has reiterated the entire version averments and contentions taken in the course of written statement in her evidence before this Court and also produced as many as Exs.R.1 and Ex.R.2 documents.
Therefore, there is no necessity to repeat those facts again.
I have gone through the documents produced by the RW-1.
Ex.R.1 is the copy of Authorization letter and Ex.R.2 is the Insurance Policy.
In the cross-examination of RW-1 by Petitioner's counsel she has deposed that she is deposing on the basis of the police records.
The offending vehicle is duly insured with the Respondent No.2 Insurance Company.

At the time of 12 SCCH - 7 M.V.C.No.9530/2024 the alleged accident the offending vehicle was following the unoffending auto and at the spot dashed against the hind portion of the unoffending auto and caused the alleged accident and the said accident is occurred as per the Ex.P-3/Spot Sketch.
Further she has denied that the alleged accident occurred due to fault of the driver of the offending vehicle.
The police has filed false Charge Sheet against the driver of the offending vehicle.
At the time of the alleged accident the insurance policy of the offending vehicle is inforce.
The said auto is third party to the offending car.
Further she has denied that in order to escape from their liability he has filed false evidence affidavit and deposing falsely.

15. On going through the Ex.P-5/Wound Certificate it is seen that the Doctor opined that in the said alleged accident the Petitioner has sustained 1) abrasion on right arm, 2) an abrasion on right forearm, 3) abrasion on right knee, 4) abrasion on right leg and Sujatha B vs Krishnakumar C on 2 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/6281331/
5 5) closed fracture with immobility, deformity, tenderness and swelling and the doctor opined that the injuries No.1 to 4 are simple in nature and injury No.5 is grievous in nature.
16.

On going through the Ex.P-2/Complaint and Ex.P- 3/Statement, it is seen that on 19.04.2024 at about 13 SCCH - 7 M.V.C.No.9530/2024 5.30 p.m.,
near Yembadi Tank, Punganuru - Ramasamudram Road, Kudurucheemanapalli, Ramasamudram Mandal, when the driver of the unoffending Auto bearing Reg. No.AP-03-X-4197 drove the same along with Petitioner and other passengers, at that time the driver of the offending Swift Dzire Car bearing Reg. No.AP-28-CD-8757 drove the same in a high speed, rash and negligent manner so as to endangering human life and dashed against the unoffending vehicle, as a result, the unoffending vehicle became turtle/upside on the middle of the road, as a result the passengers and the Petitioner has sustained grievous injuries.

Thereafter Petitioner was shifted to Government Hospital,
Punganur and for higher treatment she was shifted to Sahasra Hospital, Punganur wherein she was treated as inpatient from 19.04.2024 to 22.04.2024.
The accident occurred due to negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle.
17. Admittedly, the accused is the driver of the offending vehicle and further admitted that,
Petitioner sustained grievous injuries due to alleged accident caused by the offending vehicle in question.
The counsel for Respondent No.2 claimed that the said accused to be innocent and further the counsel for 14 SCCH - 7 M.V.C.No.9530/2024

Respondent No.2 contended that, the alleged accident occurred due to fault of the driver of the unoffending vehicle and no fault of the accused/driver of the offending vehicle, he was driving slowly and therefore he cannot be held to be negligent.

On going through the prosecution papers, FIR, Spot Sketch, Wound Certificate and Charge Sheet and the evidence of PW-1 is specific to the effect that, the driver of the offending vehicle/accused is the reason for the said incident and at her instance, the incident took place and the alleged accident was occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle and fault of the accused.

The evidence of Pw.1 is corroborated to the case of the prosecution and she has supported the manner of occurrence in her evidence in the court and the manner of occurrence is the same as alleged in the Ex.P2/Complaint and Ex.P-3/Statement.
It seems that Pw.1 has clearly made those versions, which could not be shattered in cross examination.

Therefore, considering the above discussed aspects collectively, it is the considered opinion of the Court that, the incident having been taken place in the manner asserted by the prosecution and the same being proved to have been taken place in the manner alleged by the 15 SCCH - 7 M.V.C.No.9530/2024 prosecution

,
the accused drove the offending vehicle in a high speed, rash or negligent manner so as to endanger human life and at the spot dashed against the unoffending vehicle, as a result Petitioner sustained grievous injuries.

The evidence of Pw.1, Ex.P-1/FIR, Ex.P-2/Complaint, Ex.P4/spot sketch,
Ex.P5/Wound Certificate and Ex.P-6/Charge Sheet clearly establishes that the alleged accident occurred at the spot.
It is not in dispute as to the aspect that, the Petitioner sustained grievous injuries in the alleged incident.
Because, for the above reasons collectively it is clear that, the accident happened due to rash and negligent act of the accused.
It is evident that injuries noted in the Ex.P5/Wound Certificate would be caused by a road accident.
At the same time, it has come out in evidence that the alleged accident was occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle and fault of the accused.

Matters being so, acts of the accused person clearly constitute the Sujatha B vs Krishnakumar C on 2 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/6281331/
6 offences punishable under sections 338 and 337(b) of IPC.

Thus because of such negligent act of the accused/driver of the offending vehicle, it resulted in the injuries of the innocent women/Petitioner aforesaid, as he/accused drove the said offending vehicle very rashly or negligently on the spot.
Therefore, the alleged 16 SCCH - 7 M.V.C.No.9530/2024 accident occurred due to the fault of the accused/driver of the offending vehicle.
Accordingly I answered Issue No.1 in the Affirmative.

18. Issue No.2 :- The Learned counsel for the Petitioner has contended that, the injured Petitioner was aged about 34 years and she was doing mason assistant and earning Rs.30,000/- p.m., and the Petitioner has incurred heavy expenses towards medical expenditure.

As such the Petitioner is entitled for compensation under the head of pain and suffering, mental agony, medical expenses,
special diet, conveyance, loss of future income due to disability, loss of amenities and loss of income during laid up period and prays to award the compensation as prayed in the petition.

19. On the other hand, the learned counsel for Respondent No.2 insurance company contended that even though the Petitioner claimed that her earning was about Rs.30,000/- p.m., the same is not established by the claimant by producing the documents.
Since the Petitioner has not established her income, she is not entitled for compensation towards such prospects and hence prays dismissal of the petition.

The petitioner contended that as on the date of the accident she was aged about 34 years and she relied on the Ex.P.11/Adhar Card of the Petitioner, wherein the date of birth of the Petitioner is shown as 05.05.1990 and this accident was took place on 19.04.2024.
Hence it is clear that as on the date of the accident the Petitioner was aged about 33 years 11 months.
Hence the age of the Petitioner is considered as 33 years.
21. It is not in dispute that the Petitioner sustained injuries in the road traffic accident occurred due to rash and negligent riding of the offending vehicle by its driver/accused.
In the instance case the petitioner claimed that she was doing mason assistant and earning sum of Rs.30,000/- p.m.
But she has not produced single piece of document to prove his actual income.
In the absence of proof of income the notional income has to be assessed.

As per the guidelines issued by the Karnataka State Legal Service Authority, for the accident taken place in the year 2024, the notional income of the Petitioner is taken at Rs.15,750/-.
22.

In the chief examination of PW-2/Dr.S.A. Somashekara, Orthopedic Surgeon deposed that in the alleged road traffic accident the petitioner has 18 SCCH - 7 M.V.C.No.9530/2024 sustained long spiral fracture both bones left leg and she underwent IMIL nailing for left tibia and now the Petitioner complains of pain and difficulty in walking and climbing stairs, inability to squat and sit cross legged and inability to work as a coolie worker and recent x-ray shows united fracture of both bones of left leg with implants on in situ and the Petitioner has sustained disability of right lower limb at 37% and whole body disability at 19% and the Petitioner needs surgery for removal of implants which would cost around Rs.40,000/-.
PW-2 has produced Ex.P.12/OPD Card with examination Report and Ex.P.13/X-ray Film.

In the Cross examination of PW.2/doctor by the Sujatha B vs Krishnakumar C on 2 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/6281331/
7 counsel for Respondent No.2 he has deposed that he has not a treated doctor of the Petitioner and he has assessed the disability of the Petitioner.
Prior to assessing the disability he has gone through Discharge Summary and Wound Certificate and he has not taken advice from the treated doctor.

He has assessed 37% with respect to left lower limb and in his evidence affidavit due to typographical mistake the same is wrongly typed as right lower limb and similarly due to typographical mistake or clerical error her age is wrongly written as 56 years instead of 32 years.
The fracture is united and there is no infections therein 19 SCCH - 7 M.V.C.No.9530/2024 and the implants are not removed.
For removal of implants he has estimated Rs.40,000/- towards medical expenditure and he has not given estimation letter or certificate to that extent.
Further he has denied that on considering to whole body he has to take 1/3rd.
Further he has denied that after removal of implants the disability will be reduced.
He has assessed only physical disability and he has not given disability certificate.
Further he has deposed that the Petitioner is hale and healthy and she can do her regular work and activities as past without any pain or difficulties.
Further he has denied that the Petitioner is not sustained injuries due to alleged accident.
Further he denied that in order to help the petitioner he has assessed disability on the higher side and filed false evidence affidavit and deposing falsely.

23. As the occupation of the petitioner is considered as mason work, while doing her work the petitioner has to sit and stand for long time, she has to use her hands to lift the weights and to do her regular routine activities.
But due to injuries sustained in the alleged accident, he is not in a position to do work as earlier.
The doctor stated that the Petitioner has sustained disability of right lower limb at 37% 20 SCCH - 7 M.V.C.No.9530/2024 and whole body disability at 19%.
Hence by considering the age, occupation, nature of injury and the functional disability of the petitioner is considered as 19% to the whole body.
24. With regard to the quantum, age of the petitioner is considered as 33 years and the income is considered at Rs.15,750/- p.m.
As per Sarala Varma's Case the multiplier 16 is applicable and functional disability is considered at 19%.

On considering the avocation and age of the petitioner,
the total loss of future income is calculated as (Rs. 15,750/- X 12 X 16 X 19/100) = Rs.5,74,560/-.
Hence, an amount of Rs.5,74,560/- is awarded to the petitioner under the head loss of future income for the disability suffered by him in the accident.

25. In the alleged accident, as per Ex.P5 wound certificate, the petitioner has sustained 1) abrasion on right arm, 2) an abrasion on right forearm, 3) abrasion on right knee, 4) abrasion on right leg and 5) closed fracture with immobility, deformity, tenderness and swelling and undergone surgery,
which shows that definitely the petitioner has suffered pain due to the injuries sustained in the accident, hence an amount of Rs.1,00,000/- is awarded towards pain and suffering, mental agony.
21 SCCH - 7 M.V.C.No.9530/2024 26.

Further due to the injuries sustained in the accident the petitioner has taken treatment at Sahasra Hospital wherein she was taken treatment as an inpatient from 19.04.2024 to 22.04.2024,
i.e., for 4 days.
Therefore this court deems it appropriate to award Rs.20,000/- (Rs.5,000/- X 4 days) under head of special diet and conveyance.

Sujatha B vs Krishnakumar C on 2 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/6281331/
8 27.
Due to the injuries sustained in the accident the petitioner has suffered uncomfortable in her day to day life, hence an amount of Rs.1,00,000/- is awarded towards loss of amenities.
28. Due to the injuries sustained in the accident the Petitioner would require atleast six months period to recuperate and to get back to his normal day to day activities.
Therefore the Petitioner would be entitled to Rs.94,500/- (Rs.15,750/- x 6 months) under the head loss of income during laid up period.
29. Further the Petitioner has produced hospital and medical bills, towards medical expenses as per Ex.P.10 for an amount of Rs.57,354/-.
Hence the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.57,354/- under the head of hospital and medical expenses.
In the evidence affidavit of PW-2/doctor has stated that the Petitioner needs surgery for removal of implants which would cost around Rs.40,000/-.

Hence, the Petitioner is entitled for Rs.40,000/-
compensation under the head future medical expenses.
31.

The details of compensation I propose to award are as under:
Sl. Compensation under different heads Amount in (Rs) No. 1 Loss of future income due to disability 5,74,560-00 2 Pain and suffering, mental agony 1,00,000-00 3
Special diet and conveyance 20,000-00 4 Loss of amenities 1,00,000-00 5 Loss of income during laid up period 94,500-00 6
Actual medical expenses 57,354-00 7
Future medical expenses 40,000-00 Total 9,86,414-00

The Petitioner is entitled to a total compensation of Rs.9,86,414/-.
32.
Hence the respondents No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the award amount.
However, the primary liability to pay the compensation 23 SCCH - 7 M.V.C.No.9530/2024 amount is fixed on the respondent No.2/Insurance Company and it is directed to deposit the compensation amount.
Thus I conclude that, the Insurance company/Respondent No.2 is directed to deposit the compensation amount along with interest at 6% p.a., from the date of filing of the claim petition.
Hence, I answer issue No.2 is partly in the affirmative.
33. Issue No.3:

In the result I proceed to pass the following: -
ORDER
The claim petition filed by the Petitioner under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act is hereby Partly allowed with cost.

The Petitioner is entitled for total compensation amount of Rs.9,86,414/- (Rupees Nine Lakhs Eighty Six Thousand Four Hundred and Fourteen only) with interest @
6% p.a., from the date of petition till its realization.
Amount awarded under the future medical expenses does not carry future interest.

Sujatha B vs Krishnakumar C on 2 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/6281331/
9

Further, Respondent No.2/ Insurance Company being insurer of 24 SCCH - 7 M.V.C.No.9530/2024 the offending vehicle is directed to deposit the compensation amount together with 6% interest within 60 days from the date of this order.
After deposit, entire compensation amount with interest shall be released in favour of the Petitioner under E-payment with proper verification and identification.
Advocate fee is fixed at  Rs.1,000/-.
Draw the award accordingly.

(Shyam Prakash)

opennyai_summary.facts:
1. The petitioner filed this petition under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act 1989, seeking compensation of Rs.15,00,000/- for the injures sustained by her in the road traffic accident occurred on 19.04.2024.
2.
Accordingly, a case was registered in their Crime No.87/2024 and prepared F.I.R. for the offence punishable under sections 338 and 337 of IPC and submitted to the jurisdictional judicial Magistrate and the superior officers and investigation was taken up by the investigating Officer.
The alleged accident is occurred due to fault and negligence act of the driver of the offending Maruthi Swift Dezire Car bearing Reg. No.AP-28-CD-8757.
Sujatha B vs Krishnakumar C on 2 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/6281331/
2 5.
Further it is alleged that there is no compliance of provision under Section 134(C),
158(6) of M.V. Act.
As such the insurance company is not liable to pay any compensation and in order to get compensation the Petitioner has constrained to filed the present claim petition.
Further it is denied that the age,
income and occupation of the Petitioner and the petition is false and frivolous in the eye of law and the quantum of compensation claimed by the claimants is exorbitant and reserves the right u/s.170 of M.V. Act., and violated terms and conditions of the insurance policy.
opennyai_summary.issue:
Whether the Petitioner proves that on 19-04-2024 at about 5.30 p.m., when she was going towards Punganur town from Ramasamudram town side as a passenger in a Auto Rickshaw 6 SCCH - 7 M.V.C.No.9530/2024 bearing registration No.AP-03-X-  4197 near Yemabadi Village,
 Ramasamudram Mandal,
 Annamayya district, Andhra Pradesh, at that time the driver of the said offending Maruthi Dezire Car bearing registration No.AP-28- CD-8757 drove the same in a high speed, rash and negligent manner and dashed against the said Auto Rickshaw and as a result the Auto Rickshaw capsized and she sustained grievous injuries?
2. Whether petitioner is entitled for compensation? If so, what is the quantum?
from whom?
3. What order or award?
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
The burden to prove the framed issues lies on the Petitioner.
The accident occurred due to negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle.
Petitioner sustained grievous injuries due to alleged accident caused by the offending vehicle in question.
On going through the prosecution papers, FIR, Spot Sketch, Wound Certificate and Charge Sheet and the evidence of PW-1 is specific to the effect that, the driver of the offending vehicle/accused is the reason for the said incident and at her instance, the incident took place and the alleged accident was occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle and fault of the accused.
,
the accused drove the offending vehicle in a high speed, rash or negligent manner so as to endanger human life and at the spot dashed against the unoffending vehicle, as a result Petitioner sustained grievous injuries.
Because, for the above reasons collectively it is clear that, the accident happened due to rash and negligent act of the accused.
It is evident that injuries noted in the Ex.P5/Wound Certificate would be caused by a road accident.
At the same time, it has come out in evidence that the alleged accident was occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle and fault of the accused.
Matters being so, acts of the accused person clearly constitute the Sujatha B vs Krishnakumar C on 2 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/6281331/
6 offences punishable under sections 338 and 337(b) of IPC.
Thus because of such negligent act of the accused/driver of the offending vehicle, it resulted in the injuries of the innocent women/Petitioner aforesaid, as he/accused drove the said offending vehicle very rashly or negligently on the spot.
21. It is not in dispute that the Petitioner sustained injuries in the road traffic accident occurred due to rash and negligent riding of the offending vehicle by its driver/accused.
But she has not produced single piece of document to prove his actual income.
In the absence of proof of income the notional income has to be assessed.
opennyai_summary.arguments:
Respondent No.2 contended that, the alleged accident occurred due to fault of the driver of the unoffending vehicle and no fault of the accused/driver of the offending vehicle, he was driving slowly and therefore he cannot be held to be negligent.
Since the Petitioner has not established her income, she is not entitled for compensation towards such prospects and hence prays dismissal of the petition.
The petitioner contended that as on the date of the accident she was aged about 34 years and she relied on the Ex.P.11/Adhar Card of the Petitioner, wherein the date of birth of the Petitioner is shown as 05.05.1990 and this accident was took place on 19.04.2024.
Hence it is clear that as on the date of the accident the Petitioner was aged about 33 years 11 months.
In the instance case the petitioner claimed that she was doing mason assistant and earning sum of Rs.30,000/- p.m.
Hence by considering the age, occupation, nature of injury and the functional disability of the petitioner is considered as 19% to the whole body.
opennyai_summary.decision:
Hence, an amount of Rs.5,74,560/- is awarded to the petitioner under the head loss of future income for the disability suffered by him in the accident.
Therefore this court deems it appropriate to award Rs.20,000/- (Rs.5,000/- X 4 days) under head of special diet and conveyance.
Due to the injuries sustained in the accident the petitioner has suffered uncomfortable in her day to day life, hence an amount of Rs.1,00,000/- is awarded towards loss of amenities.
28. Due to the injuries sustained in the accident the Petitioner would require atleast six months period to recuperate and to get back to his normal day to day activities.
Therefore the Petitioner would be entitled to Rs.94,500/- (Rs.15,750/- x 6 months) under the head loss of income during laid up period.
29. Further the Petitioner has produced hospital and medical bills, towards medical expenses as per Ex.P.10 for an amount of Rs.57,354/-.
Hence the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.57,354/- under the head of hospital and medical expenses.
In the evidence affidavit of PW-2/doctor has stated that the Petitioner needs surgery for removal of implants which would cost around Rs.40,000/-.
Hence, the Petitioner is entitled for Rs.40,000/-
compensation under the head future medical expenses.
31.
The details of compensation I propose to award are as under:
Sl. Compensation under different heads Amount in (Rs) No. 1 Loss of future income due to disability 5,74,560-00 2 Pain and suffering, mental agony 1,00,000-00 3
Special diet and conveyance 20,000-00 4 Loss of amenities 1,00,000-00 5 Loss of income during laid up period 94,500-00 6
Actual medical expenses 57,354-00 7
Future medical expenses 40,000-00 Total 9,86,414-00
The Petitioner is entitled to a total compensation of Rs.9,86,414/-.
32.
Hence the respondents No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the award amount.
However, the primary liability to pay the compensation 23 SCCH - 7 M.V.C.No.9530/2024 amount is fixed on the respondent No.2/Insurance Company and it is directed to deposit the compensation amount.
Thus I conclude that, the Insurance company/Respondent No.2 is directed to deposit the compensation amount along with interest at 6% p.a., from the date of filing of the claim petition.
Hence, I answer issue No.2 is partly in the affirmative.
33. Issue No.3:
In the result I proceed to pass the following: -
ORDER
The claim petition filed by the Petitioner under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act is hereby Partly allowed with cost.
The Petitioner is entitled for total compensation amount of Rs.9,86,414/- (Rupees Nine Lakhs Eighty Six Thousand Four Hundred and Fourteen only) with interest @
6% p.a., from the date of petition till its realization.
Amount awarded under the future medical expenses does not carry future interest.
Further, Respondent No.2/ Insurance Company being insurer of 24 SCCH - 7 M.V.C.No.9530/2024 the offending vehicle is directed to deposit the compensation amount together with 6% interest within 60 days from the date of this order.
After deposit, entire compensation amount with interest shall be released in favour of the Petitioner under E-payment with proper verification and identification.
Advocate fee is fixed at  Rs.1,000/-.
Draw the award accordingly.
